items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: Duke had told Bobby Boyd, the road manager, you know, to go get Dizzy Gillespie

ctx.x: I think it was on, "Jazz Party," the record, "Jazz Party," that I was on with the band, Quentin Jackson, Butter as we called him, told me -- it was on some

things there was no first trumpet part, and so Duke had -- it was a double date, you know. One date, then we had dinner, then we came back and did the second one, and when we came back, Duke had told Bobby Boyd, the road manager, you know, to go get Dizzy Gillespie, because he wanted some discipline. And he got it. When Dizzy walked in the studio, everybody was sitting up like tin soldiers, you know? But now Clarke Terry didn't have to worry about it, you know, because Clarke could handle himself. And that was…
That's a hell of a section.
